items.text: Can you explain properly what each coefficient actually measures and where they came from (who introduced them and roughly when), and say which of those two claims is right?

Calculate both r and r_s by hand with the working shown (we aren't allowed the GDC for this homework), explain why they come out different for the same data, and tell me which word I should use to describe the strength.
Our textbook says anything above 0.7 is "strong" but my teacher said "it depends" - is 0.7 an actual IB rule or just a guideline, and where does it come from? [8 marks]
